tests.procedure: Under strong white light check each received sample container separately on a clean transparent watch glass or glass dish for foreign particles, colour and conformity with the in-house visual specification.
tests.source: Ferric Ammonium Citrate__STM Ferric Ammonium Citrate 1-3.txt:30

tests.procedure: BP/USP style stepwise solubility: 100 mg powdered sample in a stoppered tube with 0.1 mL solvent, shake 1 min, hold 25.0 ± 0.5 °C for 15 min (repeat once if not dissolved); add 0.9 mL, then 2 mL, then 7 mL solvent with the same shake and hold to classify very soluble / freely soluble / soluble / sparingly soluble; if still undissolved, 10 mg in 10 mL (slightly soluble), then 1 mg in 10 mL (very slightly soluble), else practically insoluble. Repeat with ethanol (96 per cent).
tests.source: Ferric Ammonium Citrate__STM Ferric Ammonium Citrate 1-3.txt:31

tests.procedure: Identification (USP): (A) ignite about 0.5 g, it chars and leaves a residue of iron oxide. (B) to 10 mL of a 1 in 100 solution add 6 N ammonium hydroxide dropwise, the solution darkens but no precipitate forms. (C) to 5 mL of a 1 in 100 solution add 0.3 mL potassium permanganate TS and 4 mL mercuric sulphate TS, heat to boiling, a white precipitate forms.

details.B_ammoniumHydroxide: 10 mL of 1 in 100 solution; add 6 N ammonium hydroxide dropwise
details.C_permanganate: 5 mL of 1 in 100 solution; add 0.3 mL potassium permanganate TS and 4 mL mercuric sulphate TS; heat to boiling

tests.source: Ferric Ammonium Citrate__STM Ferric Ammonium Citrate 1-3.txt:32

tests.procedure: Ferric citrate: to a solution of Ferric Ammonium Citrate (1 in 100) add potassium ferrocyanide TS (1 g in 10 mL water). No blue precipitate is formed.

details.reagent: Potassium ferrocyanide TS: 1 g in 10 mL water

tests.source: Ferric Ammonium Citrate__STM Ferric Ammonium Citrate 1-3.txt:35; reagent Ferric Ammonium Citrate__STM Ferric Ammonium Citrate 1-3.txt:28

tests.procedure: Sulphates limit test (USP <221>): dissolve 100 mg sample in 1 mL 2.7 N hydrochloric acid, dilute with water to 30 mL, add 3 mL barium chloride TS, dilute to 50 mL and mix. Standard: 0.31 mL of 0.020 N sulfuric acid diluted to 30 mL, same steps. Any turbidity in the sample after 10 minutes is not greater than in the standard (0.3%).

details.sample: 100 mg dissolved in 1 mL 2.7 N hydrochloric acid, diluted to 30 mL
details.standard: 0.31 mL of 0.020 N sulfuric acid diluted to 30 mL
details.bariumChloride: 3 mL barium chloride TS (12 g in 100 mL water), diluted to 50 mL

tests.source: Ferric Ammonium Citrate__STM Ferric Ammonium Citrate 1-3.txt:33

tests.procedure: Oxalate (USP): transfer 1 g to a separator, dissolve in 10 mL water, add 2 mL hydrochloric acid, extract with 50 mL then 20 mL ether; combine the ether extracts in a 150-mL beaker, add 10 mL water and evaporate the ether on a steam bath; add 1 drop glacial acetic acid and 1 mL calcium acetate solution (1 in 20). No turbidity within 5 minutes.

details.reagent: 1 mL calcium acetate solution (1 in 20) with 1 drop glacial acetic acid

tests.source: Ferric Ammonium Citrate__STM Ferric Ammonium Citrate 1-3.txt:34

tests.procedure: Lead by AAS (USP <852>): sample 15 g dissolved in 50 mL water and 1 mL nitric acid, made up to 100 mL with water. Standard: 10.0 mL of lead stock (about 159.8 mg lead nitrate in 100 mL water with 1 mL nitric acid, diluted to 1000.0 mL) diluted to 500 mL, 2 µg lead per mL. Lead hollow-cathode lamp, air-acetylene flame. Lead content (µg/g) = 100 (C/W)(AU/AS), or the AAS software concentration.

details.sampleSolution: 15 g in 50 mL water and 1 mL nitric acid, made up to 100 mL with water
details.standardPreparation: 10.0 mL of lead stock (about 159.8 mg lead nitrate in 100 mL water with 1 mL nitric acid, to 1000.0 mL) diluted to 500 mL
details.formula: 100 (C/W)(AU/AS); C = lead concentration of standard (µg/mL), W = sample weight (g), AU and AS = absorbances of test and standard solutions

tests.source: Ferric Ammonium Citrate__STM Ferric Ammonium Citrate 1-3.txt:36

tests.procedure: Mercury by AAS, cold vapour (USP <852>, main method): transfer about 1.000 g sample to a closed centrifuge bottle, add 5 mL nitric acid and 5 mL hydrochloric acid, digest on a steam bath for 1 h, cool, transfer to a glass-stoppered bottle, dilute to 100 mL with water and bubble air 2 min; prepare a reagent blank the same way. Add 5 mL stannous chloride solution, insert the aeration apparatus immediately, read absorbances, plot against standards (2.5, 5.0, 10.0 and 35.0 µg/mL mercury) and read the concentration of the test solution. Limit NMT 10 µg/g.

details.digestion: 5 mL nitric acid + 5 mL hydrochloric acid, steam bath 1 h, closed bottle
details.standardStock: 135.4 mg mercuric chloride in 100 mL, diluted with 1 N sulfuric acid (100 mg mercury per 100 mL)
details.standardPreparation: 2.0 mL stock to 100 mL with 1 N sulfuric acid; 0.25, 0.50, 1.0 and 3.5 mL of that to 100 mL with water (as written)
details.reductant: 5 mL stannous chloride solution per solution
details.technique: cold vapour AAS with aeration apparatus; blank corrected

tests.source: Ferric Ammonium Citrate__STM Ferric Ammonium Citrate 1-3.txt:37

tests.procedure: Assay (USP, iodometric back titration of iron): transfer about 1 g sample to a 250-mL flask, dissolve in 25 mL water and 5 mL hydrochloric acid, add 4 g potassium iodide, stopper, stand 15 min protected from light; add 100 mL water and titrate the liberated iodine with 0.1 N sodium thiosulfate VS using starch TS; blank determination. Each mL of 0.1 N sodium thiosulfate = 5.585 mg iron (Fe). Assay = (E.P x eq.wt x F x 100) / W.

details.solvent: 25 mL water and 5 mL hydrochloric acid
details.titrantStandardization: about 210 mg primary standard potassium dichromate dissolved in 100 mL water, with 3 g potassium iodide, 2 g sodium bicarbonate and 5 mL hydrochloric acid, 10 min in the dark, titrated with the thiosulfate to yellowish green, 3 mL starch TS, to colourless; blank. N = mg K2Cr2O7 / (49.04 x mL Na2S2O3)
details.equivalence: each mL of 0.1 N sodium thiosulfate = 5.585 mg iron (Fe)
details.formula: Assay = (E.P x eq.wt x F x 100) / W; E.P = end point of titration, eq.wt = equivalent weight of iron, F = titrant factor, W = sample weight (mg as written)
